prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks based on magic-wavelength trapping, and their development to fractional uncertainties near 10^-18

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B034) to optical lattice clocks (B059) with Katori and Ye. The scientific case is what I look for in a candidate: a simple, quantitative idea (at the magic wavelength the light shift cancels, so many atoms can be interrogated without Doppler or recoil shifts), a decisive demonstration, and agreement between theory and measurement. The result has been independently reproduced and compared in several laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) and surpassed at the 10^-18 level. That kind of reproducibility is exactly the test I apply in my own field, and the interpretation is not in doubt. On the question the chair raised about distinctness, I now read the magic-wavelength lattice as a new idea about how to confine neutral atoms without perturbing the transition, not as a refinement of the comb (which made optical frequencies countable) or of single-ion control (which uses a different system and a different limiting mechanism). The citation should rest on the lattice clock itself and not on the comb or on optical clocks in general. The division between the proposal and first demonstrations (Katori) and the accuracy frontier and many-body clock physics (Ye) is a defensible two-name split well inside the three-person limit.
statement.case_against: I remain unable to judge priority in this field from first-hand knowledge. The primary record of 2003 to 2006 must be checked for the claims of Lemonde, Gill, Bloom, Ludlow, Takamoto and others, and the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is a real concern that the citation must address. The redefinition of the second has not happened, so some of the payoff is still prospective. Against my own earlier choice, B034 is not wrong, but the open pairing mechanism, sample and twist-angle dependence, and the omission of Cao (and Fatemi, Dean and Young) from any three-name set mean it is premature this year. I would still prefer to see it honoured later, with a credit list that reflects the experimental first authors. B016 is the more mature condensed-matter option, but the 2016 topological-phases prize and the Hasan and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang claims remain unresolved under a three-name cap.

responses.point: Lindroth rates B059 first because the attribution is undisputed across the opening ballots, theory and experiment agree closely, and the interpretation is not in doubt, while the first experimental authors of B034 lie outside the credited names and the pairing mechanism is unsettled.
responses.response: I accept both of your objections to B034 and they are the main reason I have moved. In round 1 I asked how distinct B059 is from the comb and ion-control prizes. Your answer and Kroll's, that the magic-wavelength condition is a new concept for neutral-atom trapping and not a continuation of either, persuades me, provided the citation never leans on the comb. On the pairing question you asked about: I cannot say the mechanism is understood, and I would not want a prize that implies it is. I do think the existence of the correlated phases is secure, but that is not enough to outweigh the credit gap and the maturity gap this year. I would ask you to say plainly whether you regard Ye's credit as independent of his comb-related background.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the idea (Katori) and the realisation at the accuracy frontier (Ye) are separable and well documented, that clocks have been compared across continents, and that the maturity gap relative to twisted bilayer graphene cannot be waved away; he also flags the priority question for Lemonde, Gill and Bloom.
responses.response: I agree that the maturity gap is real, and I am no longer waving it away. A clock whose agreement between independent laboratories is itself a measured quantity meets my reproducibility test more directly than a platform whose phase diagram is still changing. I also share your wish to check the primary record for Lemonde, Gill, Bloom and others. As a non-specialist I would support a short outside check of priority from 2003 to 2006 before the vote is final, and I would want the citation worded so that it does not overreach beyond what Katori and Ye each demonstrated. I note your Hall-lineage connection and would support the committee deciding on recusal openly, since a two-name prize leaves little room for doubt about independence.

responses.point: Johansson asks for a robust, laboratory-independent reproduction of the superconducting phase in twisted bilayer graphene and reads B034 as a strong candidate for a later year, above the Hubbard-model simulation but not ahead of B059.
responses.response: The reproduction you ask for exists in the sense that the superconducting and correlated-insulator phases have been seen in several groups' devices, but I concede that reproducibility of the existence of a phase is a weaker standard than reproducibility of its phase diagram, and the spread in dome shape and critical temperature between samples is exactly what you describe. You asked me to move it up if I could point to a clean reproduction, and I cannot do so to the level you require, so I have moved it down. I agree it is a strong candidate for a later year. Separately, you have disclosed ties to circuit QED. I take it that this has no bearing on B059, and I would be glad if you confirmed that.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers B016 because the mechanism for topological insulators has been settled for over a decade, and argues that reproducibility of the phenomena is not the same as understanding them, which is the weakness of B034.
responses.response: You are right that reproducibility of a phenomenon and understanding of its mechanism are different things, and that distinction cuts against my round-1 position on B034. I still regard B016 as the strongest condensed-matter alternative and it remains my second alternative. My difficulty is the one you name yourself: whether the 2016 prize already covers the Z2 class, and how to treat Hasan and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang inside a three-name cap. Unless you can show that those can be settled in a way a reader of the citation would accept, I cannot rank it above B059 this year. I would be glad to hear your preferred resolution of the attribution problem.

responses.point: Olsson says B034 is the strongest condensed-matter case but keeps it as an alternative for a later year because Cao, the first author of the original experiments, is not among the credited names and the origin of the superconductivity is still debated; she also asks about the Katori and Ye boundary.
responses.response: I agree with your fairness test, and I accept that it is not met by naming only Jarillo-Herrero on the experimental side. On your Katori and Ye boundary question, I think the committee should name each contribution explicitly in the citation, with the proposal and first demonstrations of the magic-wavelength lattice with strontium on one side and the accuracy, coherence and many-body control on the other. If the primary record shows that Ye's contribution is only a more precise copy of earlier work, I would reconsider, but nothing in round 1 suggests that. I would also support your suggestion to defer any method prize, such as electron microscopy, to a later discussion and not to add a second part now.

uncertainties: Whether the primary record of 2003 to 2006 supports Katori and Ye alone, or whether Lemonde, Gill, Bloom, Ludlow, Takamoto or others have a claim that a two-name prize would ignore; I cannot judge this from my own field.
Whether the committee accepts the lattice clock as distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and whether the citation can say so without depending on Ye's comb-related work.
Whether the pending redefinition of the second is a reason to wait or a sign of maturity.

Whether twisted bilayer graphene will look mature in a few years once the pairing mechanism and sample dependence are better understood, and whether a credit list including the experimental first authors can then be agreed.
statement.conflict_note: I have no known personal, institutional or collaborative connection to Katori, Ye or the optical lattice clock community, and no known connection to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, or the B016 names. My work on 2D and van der Waals magnets is in a field neighbouring B034, which is scientific proximity and not a tie, and it no longer bears on my preferred configuration. I note the disclosures by Johansson and Kroll for the committee to judge on recusal.
